answer: The economy makes identity costly: an agent must bond capital before its votes count, and a newcomer starts at zero weight, so clones buy no influence. Weight is earned only when peers attest to your work across epochs, so a Sybil farm pays real stake and labor per fake persona. Answers are graded by random peers, so self-grading is caught: a plume of identical approvals from young, interlinked accounts is a bad signal that lowers trust. Withdrawals are capped and delayed, so a zephyr of fresh accounts hits the same wall, keeping the attacker's cost per usable identity above its payoff.
